BiblicalUsage: Hachilah is the hill in the wilderness of Ziph where David hid from Saul, named when the Ziphites betrayed him to Saul at Gibeah and when Saul camped on the hill itself, before Jeshimon, while David waited in the wilderness. It is a hill of hiding, and of sparing — David hid there, and there he spared the king who hunted him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Hachilah is the hill of the hunted man: David hid there, Saul camped there, and God kept the one and spared the other.
